question: Where can I get electricity consumption by municipality or postal code in the United States, by sector and year?

answer.summary: No national dataset: EIA-861 gives sales (MWh) by utility, state and sector, and only lists counties served. Local metered data exist state by state: New York's Utility Energy Registry gives monthly MWh by city/town/village and sector (ZIP only for NYC) via open API; PG&E publishes monthly kWh by ZIP and customer type (download behind a form); some utilities send cities annual reports (e.g. Xcel). ZIP codes are not Census ZCTAs.
main_caveats: No federal source gives municipal or ZIP consumption; EIA-861 is by utility and state, and its county list is service territory without sales.
Local data are privacy-screened: withheld sectors (NY -999), merged ZIPs (PG&E) or merged classes (Xcel).
USPS ZIP codes used by utilities are delivery-based and differ from Census ZCTAs and from municipal boundaries.
Utility totals cover only that utility's customers; municipalities served by several utilities need all of them.
answer.confidence_reason: NY registry fully tested via API and EIA checked; California tested only at page level (form), other states sampled with one Xcel report.

attributes.note: Metered MWh/kWh in NY (statewide municipalities), PG&E ZIPs and Xcel city reports; no national local-level series.
attributes.gap_note: Only NY, PG&E (CA) and one Xcel city tested; EIA-861 checked and stops at utility-state level; other states' registries or utility programs not searched.

attributes.note: NY: municipality name, type and FIPS (ZIP only NYC); PG&E: USPS ZIP, merged with neighbours below thresholds; Xcel: city.
attributes.gap_note: Municipal/ZIP geography verified only in the sampled sources; boundary changes not documented in them.

attributes.note: NY: R, C, I, C+I, Total with -999 withheld; PG&E: residential, commercial, agricultural, industrial; Xcel: C, I, R or 'Business'.
attributes.gap_note: Classifications differ by publisher; only sampled sources checked.

attributes.note: Year and month of consumption per row (NY, PG&E); data year stated in Xcel reports.
attributes.gap_note: Only sampled sources checked; NY has half-year gaps by utility.

attributes.note: NY to June 2026; PG&E file 2026 Q3 listed.
attributes.gap_note: PG&E latest file not opened because the download requires a form with personal details; other states not checked.

attributes.note: NY 2016-2020 (old protocol) and 2021-2026; PG&E quarterly files from 2013.
attributes.gap_note: Comparability across NY's 2021 protocol change and PG&E's early files not verified; other states not checked.

attributes.note: NY posting semi-annually; PG&E quarterly, 15 days after quarter end.

sources.name: Utility Energy Registry (UER) Monthly Community / ZIP Code / County Energy Use
sources.publisher: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA), data reported by utilities under NY PSC Case 17-M-0315
sources.summary: Official New York dataset of metered monthly electricity consumption (MWh) by city/town/village and by residential, commercial, industrial and total, reported by regulated utilities under PSC order; open API, 2021 to June 2026 (archive 2016-2020).
sources.coverage_note: New York State only; ZIP-code level only for New York City.
caveats: Half-year gaps by utility: check months before summing a year.

example.example_request: https://data.ny.gov/resource/4txm-py4p.json?$select=month,uer_id,value,number_of_accounts&$where=com_name='Albany' AND com_type='City' AND data_field='3_nat_consumption' AND year=2025&$order=month

sources.name: PG&E Energy Data Request Program public data sets: Electric Usage by ZIP
sources.publisher: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under CPUC Decision 14-05-016
sources.summary: PG&E publishes metered monthly kWh by ZIP code and customer type (residential, commercial, agricultural, industrial), quarterly CSV files 2013-2026 Q3, under CPUC privacy aggregation rules.
sources.coverage_note: PG&E territory only; similar CPUC-ordered programs at other California utilities not checked.
caveats: Download requires a form with name and email.
Small ZIPs are merged with neighbours.

problems: Download is behind a form asking for organization, name and email and acceptance of CPUC D.14-05-016 terms; not submitted.

sources.name: Utility community energy reports and town-level energy portals (sample)
sources.publisher: Utilities and energy-efficiency program administrators (Xcel Energy; Mass Save program administrators)
sources.format: PDF reports; Power BI web app
sources.summary: Some utilities give cities annual community energy reports (e.g. Xcel Energy: kWh and customers by commercial, industrial, residential; tested Robbinsdale, MN, 2022), published as PDFs by cities.
sources.coverage_note: Scattered, city by city; not a dataset.
caveats: Only the utility's own customers in the city.

problems: Mass Save Data is a JavaScript application; masssave.com returned 403 to non-browser clients.

example.example_result: Commercial 381 customers 36,604,358 kWh; Industrial 29 customers 8,379,633 kWh; Residential 6,720 customers 45,195,965 kWh (Year of Data: 2022)

members_summary.scope_note: Universe unknown: utilities that produce community-level reports or portals. Tested Xcel Energy (one city report) and Mass Save Data (Massachusetts); others not checked.
members_summary.pattern: Search city sustainability or GreenStep pages for '<utility> Community Energy Report'; check state efficiency program portals.

if_unstructured.summary: Outside New York and the California utility programs, local consumption appears in utility community reports given to cities (PDF).

local_terms.meaning: New York registry of utility-reported community energy use on data.ny.gov.
CPUC-ordered utility program publishing usage by ZIP code in California (D.14-05-016).
Utility report of a city's annual energy use by customer class (e.g. Xcel Energy).
EIA-861 term for retail electricity sales by utility, state and sector.
Census ZIP Code Tabulation Area, an areal approximation of USPS ZIP codes; not identical to ZIP codes.
Privacy thresholds for releasing aggregated customer usage (PG&E: 100 residential, 15 non-residential, 15% share).
